newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazilian real remains calm, rises 0.01 pct.
newsitem.headline: Brazilian real remains calm, rises 0.01 pct.

text.p: Brazil's real closed at 1.0807 per dollar, up 0.01 percent and remaining calm in the commercial foreign exchange market despite volatility in local stocks, dealers said.
A strong recovery in the stock market, which dipped 8.5 percent on Tuesday, supported the real in the spot forex market and helped dollar contracts to fall in the futures market, dealers added.
At 1635 local/1935 GMT, preliminary figures for commercial and financial forex contracts showed a $20 million surplus, and dealers speculated the final figures could show a larger surplus.

The real did not rise further because banks decided to hold dollars in anticipation of another decline in the reais-dollar mini-band in coming days. The Central Bank devalues the mini-band about five or six times a month.

The current mini-band was set on Friday at between 1.0800 and 1.0850 reais per dollar. So far this month, the mini-band has fallen 0.33 percent against the dollar compared to monthly declines of between 0.57 and 0.61 percent in the past six months.
In the interbank floating rate market, the real dropped 0.06 percent to close at 1.0867 per dollar due to an increase in dollar outflows, traders said.
In the parallel market, the real dropped 0.26 percent to end the day at 1.143 per dollar.
